title: Seafarer killed in suspected missile strike on Gulf tanker as Trump weighs new Iran strikes
dek: A crew member died on the Greek-managed Velos Sapphire, Iran said it shot down two US drones, and Qatar's emir urged Trump to avoid escalation while Tehran's envoy took a letter to Putin.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
A seafarer was killed in an explosion believed to have been caused by a missile on an oil products tanker in the Gulf, the ship's Greek manager said on Friday, as President Donald Trump weighed whether to resume strikes on Iran and Qatar's emir urged him to avoid escalation.

Velos Tankers, based in Athens, said it was "greatly saddened" to report the death of one of its seafarers on the Marshall Islands-flagged Velos Sapphire, which was sailing without cargo towards Bahrain when the explosion happened on Thursday. The crew member was first reported missing and then found fatally injured on board, the company said. No one else was hurt, the crew put out the fire and no pollution was reported; the ship was taken to Bahrain's Khalifa Bin Salman Port and an investigation will be launched, it said. The company did not give the seafarer's nationality, and no one has said who fired at the ship.

## Friday evening: warnings and phone calls

By Friday evening, Iran's armed forces had added new warnings. The army's spokesman, Mohammad Akraminia, said renewed US attacks would bring retaliation against American military assets beyond the Middle East, according to reports. A spokesman for the aerospace arm of the Revolutionary Guards had said a day earlier that any country or force that helps the US attack Iran "can be a legitimate target", reports said.

Iran's foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, kept up his calls to the region. He spoke to the foreign ministers of the United Arab Emirates and Saudi Arabia and to Egypt's foreign minister, Badr Abdelatty, who urged "flexibility and compromise", according to reports. Oman and Iran discussed practical arrangements to restore safe navigation through the strait, while Tehran repeated that the waterway would not fully reopen until Washington met its conditions. No new US strike was announced on Friday.

In Washington, Republican congressman Thomas Massie said he would seek a House vote next week on impeaching Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth over the war, reports said; Mr Hegseth rejected the effort. Etihad Airways extended cancellations of its Abu Dhabi flights to Riyadh and Dammam until 19 November, and Iranian airlines' flights to and from the UAE remain suspended.

## A death at sea

It is not clear whether the Velos Sapphire is the tanker that the UK Maritime Trade Operations centre said on Thursday had been hit by two unidentified projectiles about 50 nautical miles north of Madinat ash Shamal in Qatar (see below). The UK naval agency said this week there had been at least 30 attacks on commercial vessels in the region in October, a record, according to reports.

Iran's Revolutionary Guards also said on Friday they had shot down two US MQM-170 reconnaissance drones over Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, according to Iranian state media; the US has not commented, and the claim has not been independently confirmed. Iraq has raised radiation monitoring along its border with Iran as a precaution, reports said, and Saudi Arabia's air defences intercepted two ballistic missiles fired by the Houthis towards Najran, a spokesman for the Saudi-led coalition said.

## Diplomacy: Doha and Moscow

Qatar's emir urged President Donald Trump on Friday to avoid further escalation with Iran, as Tehran's top security official carried a letter from Iran's supreme leader to President Vladimir Putin in Moscow while US officials, according to reports, said Mr Trump was weighing whether to resume strikes.

Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani spoke to Mr Trump by phone about Qatar's mediation towards "a comprehensive agreement to end the regional crisis", a statement from Doha said, according to reports. The emir stressed the importance of avoiding further escalation, keeping the Strait of Hormuz open to shipping and securing energy supplies, according to the statement. The call came a day after Mr Trump met his national security team to decide whether to resume full military operations against Iran, senior US officials told reporters, and after Tehran said it had sent Washington a nuclear proposal through Qatar but would not discuss it until seven conditions were met.

## Friday: Moscow, Doha and the strait

The Kremlin confirmed that Mr Putin met Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, on Thursday, but its spokesman Dmitry Peskov gave no details, according to reports from Moscow. Iranian state media said Mr Rezaei handed over a letter from Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, whose contents were not disclosed, reports said. Mr Rezaei told Iranian media the two discussed regional security after the war and gas pipelines from Russia to Iran, and that Mr Putin had said Russia was ready to help end the war; the Kremlin has not confirmed that account. Russia and Iran signed a strategic partnership treaty in January 2025, but it has no mutual defence clause.

Early on Friday, the Revolutionary Guards said two oil tankers had caught fire after hitting mines while using "unauthorised" routes through the strait, according to reports citing Iranian state media. The ships were not named, it was not clear whether this was the same incident the Guards described on Thursday, and the claim has not been independently confirmed.

For India, the stakes are oil and shipping. About 13% of the Gulf crude that passed through Hormuz in October went to India, according to data from the analytics firm Kpler cited in reports. An Iranian MP said this week that Indian ships may pass, but must pay transit fees.

## Oil

Oil, which had fallen sharply after Tuesday's US midterm elections on hopes of a deal, jumped again on Thursday. Brent crude settled at $98.29 a barrel, up nearly 4%, and US crude at $90.52, reports said, after fresh attacks on tankers in and around the strait. For India, which relies on imported crude, that rebound undoes much of the relief of earlier in the week.

## Trump's options

Speaking in the Oval Office on Thursday, Mr Trump said: "I would rather not destroy the rest of the country if possible, but maybe I will have to. You'll know soon enough," according to reports. He also questioned whether the conflict was still a war, saying "there hasn't been anybody killed in many months", and said of Iran's nuclear programme: "They're not doing anything without our approval."

One report, citing US officials, said that he is weighing three options: new strikes, continuing to squeeze Iran's economy through the US naval blockade of its ports, or a deal that would include significant concessions. A US official told reporters that Central Command was finalising preparations to resume major combat operations but had not received a new order. US officials noted that the new moon on 9 November would mean little moonlight, conditions they described as favourable for military operations, another report said.

Mr Rezaei set out Tehran's position during his visit to Moscow. "As long as they do not execute our seven conditions, we will neither open the Strait of Hormuz nor have negotiations," he said, according to reports. A senior Iranian official told reporters that a nuclear proposal had been passed to the US through Qatar and that Washington was reviewing it. The full list of conditions has not been published; Reports said they include the lifting of US sanctions, the release of frozen Iranian assets and war reparations. Washington has said nuclear issues must be part of any first round of negotiations.

## Attacks at sea

The fighting at sea did not stop. Iran's Revolutionary Guards said on Thursday that two oil tankers and a tugboat had caught fire in the strait and that another tanker had hit a mine east of it, reports said; the Guards' accounts have not been independently confirmed. The UK Maritime Trade Operations centre separately reported that a tanker was hit by two unidentified projectiles about 50 nautical miles north of Madinat ash Shamal in Qatar. The crew's condition and the extent of the damage were not known.

Oman said it was still working with Iran on a joint mechanism to control traffic through the strait, which it said could "end the state of war", according to reports. Russia's foreign ministry told its citizens not to travel to Iran, citing the "risk of a new escalation".

## Background

The war began on 28 February, when the US and Israel attacked Iran; Iran struck back at Israel and at Gulf states that host US bases, and has since restricted shipping through Hormuz. A US strike on an anti-aircraft site on Iran's Qeshm Island on election night was the first in the area since June. Vice President JD Vance has blamed the war for the Republicans' midterm defeat and has urged an agreement, while Democrats, who won both houses of Congress, have said they could use spending bills to press for an end to it.

## What happens next

Mr Trump has said a decision will come soon. A third US aircraft carrier group, led by the USS Theodore Roosevelt, is due in Singapore on Friday and is not expected in the Middle East for at least two more weeks, a US official told reporters; officials told reporters the two carrier groups already in the region were sufficient. Qatari mediators are continuing indirect talks.
